{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRCof88AAAABZfKZGA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn7ElzhDGWDI", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn7El", "number": 67, "title": "Implement channel-3 per-operator frequency selection in the shared OPN/OPNA core", "body": "## Problem

Channel 3 cannot produce independently pitched operators. [`Opn::sample`](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/637972d2c74de79355f823dfc5c46bb80a2a8f72/src/sound.rs#L195) computes one frequency from A2h/A6h and passes it to all four operators. A8h–AAh/ACh–AEh are stored but never used for synthesis, and register 27h's channel-mode bits do not affect frequency selection.

This is missing FM hardware behavior in the existing Ap sound path. It can be implemented using the current operators, algorithms and audio transport without another subsystem prerequisite.

## Expected outcome

Implement the frequency-selection portion of channel-3 special operation in the shared OPN/OPNA core.

The hardware contract is:

- With register 27h D7:D6 = `00`, all four channel-3 operators use A2h/A6h.
- Both documented nonnormal encodings, `01` and `10`, permit separate operator frequencies. Implement their common frequency selection; this Issue does not implement CSM timer-driven keying.
- Use the following bank-zero mapping, expressed in logical operator order:

| Operator | F-number low | Block/F-number high |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | A9h | ADh |
| 2 | AAh | AEh |
| 3 | A8h | ACh |
| 4 | A2h | A6h |

F-number is 11 bits; block is three bits. Program high before low. Normal operation ignores the extra frequency pairs. These contracts come from Yamaha's [YM2608 Application Manual, §§2-2-2, 2-4-1 and 2-8-4](https://csclub.uwaterloo.ca/~pbarfuss/YM2608J_Translated.PDF#page=20). The [YM2203 manufacturer datasheet, register descriptions (10), (19) and (20)](https://bitsavers.org/components/yamaha/YM2203_198911.pdf#page=5) establishes the corresponding OPN registers.

Keep existing operator multiplication, approximate detune/envelopes and algorithm routing. Switching frequency selection must not manufacture key edges or reset active operators. Channels 1–2 and 4–6 retain their ordinary frequency selection; upper-bank writes must not alias channel 3.

Scope excludes CSM automatic key-on/off, prescaler changes, frequency-write latch timing, key scaling, SSG-EG, LFO, stereo output, rhythm and ADPCM. Combined mode encoding `11` is outside this Issue's verified subset and must remain explicitly unverified. Do not claim either named special mode is fully implemented merely because its frequency selection works.

## Context and reproduction

Baseline: `637972d2c74de79355f823dfc5c46bb80a2a8f72`; supplied open-Issue list is empty. No supplied completed improvement covers this behavior.

A focused reproduction can configure channel 3 with algorithm 7, feedback/detune zero, multiplier one, immediate attack and a sustained single keyed operator. Set A6h/A2h to block 4, F-number 0600h, and ADh/A9h to block 4, F-number 0200h. Select register 27h = 40h with timers stopped, then key only operator 1 through register 28h. Current source selects the normal 0600h frequency; expected operator-1 frequency is one third of that. Repeat with 80h to test the common frequency-selection behavior separately from automatic CSM keying.

Existing [`tests/ap.rs`](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/637972d2c74de79355f823dfc5c46bb80a2a8f72/tests/ap.rs#L269), [`tests/sound86.rs`](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/637972d2c74de79355f823dfc5c46bb80a2a8f72/tests/sound86.rs) and `tests/music.rs` cover selected normal FM, algorithm, timer, bank and guest-music behavior. They do not establish special frequency selection.

Project progress: the Coordinator reports 271 native integration passes and 98 production release-Wasm browser passes for [PR #66](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/pull/66), including preserved game regressions. Independent review and remote CI evidence were not supplied. This evaluator inspected source, diffs and reports; it executed no builds or tests and changed no files.

Retain all 26 inventory categories and their full fixed scopes: partial `cpu-v30`, `cpu386`, `protected-mode`, `memory`, `pic`, `pit`, `dma`, `rtc`, `keyboard`, `mouse`, `fdc`, `gdc`, `egc`, `pegc`, `text-cg`, `display-timing`, `opn`, `opna`, `pcm86`, `bios`, `lio`, `integration`; implemented_unverified `ide`, `grcg`; unimplemented `paging`, `fpu`. No status is promoted by this plan.

After this Issue, OPN still requires CSM timer keying, combined-mode acceptance, frequency-write sequencing, prescalers, key scaling, fuller envelopes/SSG and broader synthesis verification. OPNA additionally retains LFO, pan/stereo, rhythm and ADPCM gaps. VM sound exposure remains outstanding. Protected execution, paging and basic x87 remain required. Limited probes do not establish full hardware accuracy or commercial compatibility.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Add an original Rust reproduction that fails against the baseline through observable PCM output, then passes after implementation. Record the actual before/after result.
- [ ] Add focused `opn_ch3_` tests covering all four operators independently under algorithm 7, normal selection and each nonnormal encoding with Timer A stopped. Use distinct F-numbers and blocks so swapped slots, ignored upper bits and shared-frequency shortcuts fail. Include F-number zero, high-bit boundaries and block changes. Quantitatively check pitch against an independently calculated expectation with explicit tolerances; register readback or nonzero audio alone is insufficient.
- [ ] Check normal→special→normal transitions while keyed, retained programmed frequencies, unchanged key-edge counts and continued phase/envelope progression. Check unaffected channels, upper-bank isolation, existing board masks, per-instance isolation and Machine reset. Preserve timer load/reset/IRQ behavior when other register-27 bits change.
- [ ] Add an original MIT assembly probe with offline preparation, explicit source/license/build provenance and a checked source/boot/image manifest. It must program the chip through guest instructions and produce distinguishable normal/special/operator stages. Use no proprietary ROMs, samples or acquired guest software.
- [ ] Boot the identical probe natively and through production release Wasm at `/` and `/pc98-rust/`, before and after reset, within a declared maximum of 2,000,000 instruction slots per boot. Capture stage-specific PCM through the existing audio interface and assert operator-specific pitches, normal-mode controls and finite bounded samples. Guest markers identify execution stages; they must not substitute for host PCM assertions. Hosts may load, step, provide ordinary input, reset and observe, but must not patch results or inject sound-register state. Assert guards, unchanged disk bytes and absence of guest/core/browser errors. Drain audio often enough to avoid the existing bounded queue hiding failures.
- [ ] Wire probe preparation into acceptance CI and document executable commands, including `python3 tools/prepare_opn_ch3_fixture.py` and `cargo test --locked --test ap opn_ch3_`. Keep generated assets outside the publication tree.
- [ ] The Coordinator runs the applicable [README prerequisites and checks](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/637972d2c74de79355f823dfc5c46bb80a2a8f72/README.md#reproduce-the-checks), including `cargo test --locked`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, `git diff --check` and `npm test`. Preserve existing Rust hardware, DOS/application, VM, music/PCM and six-game assertions and budgets. Report exact outcomes and any serving-port substitution without weakening tests.
- [ ] Update hardware/compatibility documentation and validation evidence to distinguish implemented frequency selection from remaining special-mode behavior. Keep OPN and OPNA partial and all inventory scopes intact. Complete repository review and resolve blocking findings before merge.

## Optional validation

None.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
